retrievalDesign.statement: Route-level composite counts and the records that entered screening are two different things, and this artifact keeps them apart. The six PubMed composites of search-strategy section 5 were executed and their counts recorded, but the records behind them were not all downloaded: S1 through S4 alone return 11,765 records unfiltered, which one session cannot screen record by record with a recorded reason each.
retrievalDesign.rule: R-RULE-1. The record set that enters screening is defined by six PubMed retrieval strata plus the complete yield of the Europe PMC fly-family route, the ClinicalTrials.gov Essie route, ten quoted-phrase OpenAlex probes, and the two preprint routes. Every stratum is a reproducible Boolean whose exact string, count and retrieved total are recorded here, and every record it returned was retrieved and given a terminal state.
retrievalDesign.preSpecification: The strata were defined and their counts measured before any record title or abstract was opened. The ordering is visible in this artifact: the stratum receipts carry the same execution date as the composite receipts, and the screening-flow artifact carries no decision that precedes them.
retrievalDesign.residual: The difference between a composite count and the records retrieved from it is a real recall gap, not a rounding error. It is quantified per route in coverageGaps and repeated as limitation L-1 in the synthesis. This pass is a prototype of the pipeline, not an exhaustive systematic review, and no claim in this task may be read as resting on an exhaustive search.

cochrane.statement: C1 was not executed. The narrow, client-specific and dated fact is this: on 2026-09-13, from a scripted client sending only the project identifier as its User-Agent, https://www.cochranelibrary.com/ returned HTTP 412 with a cookie-gate page and https://www.cochranelibrary.com/search-manager-help returned HTTP 200. No user-agent substitution was attempted, and the help page was not mined for syntax. The reason C1 was not executed is not that the edge blocked this client: it is that CENTRAL Search Manager is an interactive, subscription-gated interface for which this project has no session, and search-strategy section 6.2 already records that no public API exists for it.
cochrane.consequence: Trial coverage in this pass rests on E1, T1 and O1. CENTRAL aggregates hand-searched and registry trial records that MEDLINE indexing can miss, so the recall loss is real and is carried as limitation L-2.

pubmedComposites.statement: S1 returned 1,646 records unfiltered and 1,303 with the humans filter; S2 returned 2,597 and 2,190; S3 returned 3,739 and 2,871; S4 returned 3,783; S5 returned 53; S6 returned 418. The six retrieval strata pulled 911 PubMed records into screening. The strata are deliberately narrower than the composites and the difference is the recall this pass did not exercise.

coverageGaps.languages: No language exclusion was applied. Thirty-nine non-English records were retrieved. Two were read through the documented translation ladder (a German case report and a Portuguese mechanical analysis); six remain awaiting-full-text because no lawful full text or authorised English version was obtained, so the ladder could not be started. Search-strategy assumption SA2 still holds: every route uses English terms, so a study with no English title or abstract was probably never retrieved at all.
coverageGaps.publisherBlocks: Wiley (onlinelibrary.wiley.com), Elsevier and ScienceDirect, MDPI PDF and the NATA journals platform returned HTTP 403 or an interstitial page to this scripted client. No workaround was attempted. Records behind those blocks whose only eligible contribution needs the full text are recorded as awaiting-full-text.

platformFindings.finding: PubMed proximity distance 0 matches its two terms adjacent in either order, so "machine fly"[tiab:~0] retrieves records containing "on-the-fly machine learning". Thirty-nine records in this pass were retrieved by that artefact alone and are excluded under the new code E-REC-5.
platformFindings.evidence: The 30-term fly-family stratum N-RS1 returned 77 PubMed records, of which 25 are materials-science or computer-science papers whose abstracts contain the phrase "on-the-fly machine learning". This also explains the inflated "machine fly"[tiab:~0] index diagnostic of 32 recorded in the SBLA-008 strategy.
platformFindings.recommendation: Replace "machine fly"[tiab:~0] with an ordered form or drop it and rely on "pec deck", "pectoral deck" and the explicit fly spellings. Route to Codex and to the next evidence round; this role does not own the SBLA-008 strategy file.

platformFindings.finding: The SBLA-008 transport rule holds and extends. Unanchored S2 measured 4,098 characters of full GET URL and returned HTTP 200 on GET; the same string with the humans filter measured 4,129 characters and returned HTTP 414 on GET and HTTP 200 on POST; with the humans and adult filters it measured 4,157 characters, again 414 on GET and 200 on POST.

platformFindings.recommendation: The 3,700-character operating threshold remains conservative and correct. The observed boundary recorded at scope time (4,121 passing, 4,122 failing) is consistent with these measurements.
